title: Probabilistic contract-change oracle for JSON field regressions
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: detect and attribute quality regressions that affect JSON-structured outputs to configuration and model changes using a probabilistic, per-field approach. Motivation: deterministic schemalinting flags syntactic violations but misses subtle distributional shifts (enum skew, numeric drift, probability mass reallocation between mutually exclusive fields) caused by model hops, quantization, or routing policy changes. Proposal: build an 'oracle' that computes posterior predictive bands per-field and per-cohort, scores surprise for new traffic, and correlates spikes with recent config/model diffs. The system will integrate with shadow traffic runs and canary rollouts, provide rollback suggestions, and push alerts to Console and Slack.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Per-field probabilistic score computed for production samples and stored as time-series; 2) Alerts triggered when field surprise exceeds configurable threshold and ROC-style precision@N meets baseline; 3) Automated attribution links to recent model/config diffs and top-3 suspect changes; 4) Works in shadow mode for dedicated clusters; 5) Dashboard tile in Console showing field-level surprises and confidence intervals; 6) Runbook created with triage and rollback guidance.
design_notes: We will use lightweight Bayesian estimators (Dirichlet-multinomial for categorical enums, Gaussian/Student-t with variance adaptation for numeric fields). For nested objects and optional fields, use hierarchical smoothing and missingness modeling. Correlation attribution uses simple conditional independence checks plus a delta-lift measure: compare surprise distributions before/after a config change and compute weighted likelihood ratio. Integrations: telemetry ingestion via existing evals pipeline, artifacts in Confluence, and a staged rollout through canary lanes.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): prototype per-field estimators and a batch scoring job that consumes sampling exports; Phase 2 (2 sprints): realtime scoring hook in the streaming ingestion path, alerting rules, and a basic Console dashboard; Phase 3 (1 sprint): integrate config-diff correlator, automated rollback suggestion scoring, and on-call runbook. Key PRs and artifacts: GH draft https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pulls/1863, Confluence spec https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Probabilistic+Contract+Oracle.
metrics: signal_precision@10, false_positive_rate_weekly, time_to_detect_median, percent_regressions_attributed, cost_per_hour (batch vs realtime), end-to-end latency for scoring.
